topbar.maxAgeHint: Hide spots older than this everywhere — Spots, Bandmap and alert hits. Empty / 0 = show all.
topbar.sendTargetHint: Which node the send-panels (post spot, mail, talk, chat, sh/* queries, filters, WWV/announce posts) target when more than one is online.
conn.title: Cluster profiles
conn.rbnTagTitle: Reverse Beacon Network raw feed — skimmer spots only
conn.rbnEditorNote: Command-less skimmer firehose; only spots of your own callsign are kept. Port 7000 = CW/RTTY, 7001 = FT8/FT4.
conn.pskrHint: Real-time reception reports of your own callsign from PSK Reporter, shown on the map's “reports of me” layer. Digital modes only (FT8/FT4/RTTY/PSK…); use the RBN feed for CW. Off unless you enable it here.
conn.empty: No profile yet. Add a Telnet cluster node (e.g. host hrd.wa9pie.net, port 8000).
conn.name: Name / id
conn.autoConnect: Connect automatically when the app starts
conn.locatorHint: Used for beam heading and distance to each spot.
conn.mailWatchHint: While connected, re-check the mailbox every 10 minutes and flag new messages with a dot on the Mail tab plus a desktop notification.
conn.wsjtxHint: Adds the stations your WSJT-X decodes to the spot list (spotter “WSJT-X”), so alerts can fire on them. Point WSJT-X at this address in Settings → Reporting → UDP Server. Digital modes only; off unless you enable it here. For coexistence with JTAlert/GridTracker use a multicast address (e.g. 239.255.0.1:2237) on both.
conn.ctyCredit: DXCC data from country-files.com — thank you!
conn.presetIntro: Pick a country to see its public cluster nodes, then click one to fill in the form.
conn.presetCredit: Node list courtesy of dxcluster.info, used with permission — thank you!
conn.presetOtherSoftware: {sw} — no dedicated support; will be set up as DXSpider
spots.searchPlaceholder: search — e.g. dx:HA band:20m -mode:ft  or  "med games"
bandmap.zoomHint: Ctrl + mouse wheel over the bandmap, or drag the slider
bandmap.legendHint: Dot = the spot's own mode. The tinted band behind it is the usual mode segment (band-plan hint).
bandmap.sosHint: {freq} MHz — IARU Region 1 global emergency frequency (courtesy calling point for disaster/emergency traffic, not an official distress frequency)
bandmap.ibpHint: {freq} MHz — NCDXF/IARU International Beacon Project frequency
map.projAzimuthalHint: Azimuthal equidistant, centred on your QTH — beam headings are straight lines and distances are true.
map.projRectHint: Equirectangular world map — the whole globe at a glance.
map.noQth: Set your QRA locator in the Connection panel for a QTH-centred map and range rings.
map.mufLegendHint: MUF(3000 km). Measured from GIRO/INGV ionosondes (prop.kc2g.com) where a station is near — faint areas are the sunspot-number model filling gaps (no sporadic-E, storms or seasonal effects). Read the colour at your path's midpoint.
qh.title: Search syntax
qh.dx: DX callsign — matches from the start
qh.by: spotter callsign — matches from the start
qh.dxcc: DX country — name text or primary prefix
qh.zone: CQ / ITU zone — number, 14-16 range, or > <
qh.cont: continent — EU, NA, AS, AF, SA, OC, AN
qh.mode: mode — cw, ssb, digi, fm, or a sub-mode (ft8, rtty, sstv…)
qh.grid: grid square — matches from the start
qh.re: regular expression over call / spotter / comment
qh.byNote: by-prefixed forms (bycq, byitu, bycont, bydxcc) test the spotter side instead of the DX.
qh.bare: matches call, spotter, comment or country name
qh.grey: DX is in the sunrise/sunset grey line right now
qh.or: alternatives — a spot matches either side
qh.quote: keep spaces together (also as a value: c:"…")
qh.exBands: 20 or 40 m, spotted in the last 15 minutes
qh.exEaf: Spain or France, skimmer spots excluded
col.subject: subject
filters.title: Spot filters
filters.intro: Rules always apply locally (toggle on the Spots tab). Set a rule's scope to "local + node" to also push it as a DXSpider accept/reject spot command — mode, continent and skimmer never leave the app, they're local-only.
filters.nodeIntro: This list shows rules created in the app; use the button below to fetch filters set on the node earlier (by another client or by hand).
filters.none: No filter. All spots are shown.
filters.noNodeFilter: no active spot filter on the node
filters.clearNodeHint: Sends clear/spot all — removes every spot accept/reject rule on the node (yours and anyone else's set on this connection).
filters.clearUnsupported: The node didn't recognise the clear command — remove them by hand on the Raw terminal tab.
filters.scopeHint: "Local only" never touches the node — this rule just filters your own view. "Local + node" also applies it as a DXSpider accept/reject spot rule.
filters.localOnlyNote: Local filter only — never sent to the node.
ann.title: Announcements
ann.imported: {n} new line(s) from the node history
ann.searchPlaceholder: filter — words to keep, -word to hide (e.g. -telnet)
prop.title: Propagation (WWV / WCY)
prop.noWwv: No WWV broadcast yet (arrives every 3 hours).
prop.searchPlaceholder: filter — words to keep, -word to hide (e.g. -boulder)
prop.note: WWV/WCY broadcasts arrive live on the stream (WWV every 3 hours, WCY from DK0WCY). The button above requests a history table from the node (sh/wwv, sh/wcy) — a later phase parses it into the history too.
talk.pick: Pick a conversation, or enter a callsign.
talk.note: Talk messages arrive live; sent and received messages are stored, so conversations survive a restart.
chat.noneJoined: You are not in any group yet.
chat.note: Chat is the DXSpider conference system (JOIN/LEAVE/CHAT). Joined groups are re-joined automatically on every (re)connect.
mail.title: Mail / Bulletins
mail.pick: Pick a message, or write a new one.
mail.subject: Subject
mail.asciiWarn: Contains accented / non-ASCII characters. Many cluster nodes are ASCII-only and will garble them.
mail.notifyBody: A new message is waiting on the cluster.
mail.note: Sending drives the DXSpider interactive flow (SP/SB → subject → body → /EX). If the node uses different prompts, follow along on the Raw terminal tab.
tools.title: Tools / Queries
tools.notSupported: The "{cmd}" command is not known on this node (varies by node).
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.cooldownNote: Desktop notification (+ sound) on a matching new spot. At most once per callsign every 5 minutes.
alerts.noHits: Nothing has fired yet. Matching spots land here so they aren't lost when the live table scrolls.
alerts.hitAgeNote: age limit: set "max age" in the top bar
alerts.andNote: Within a rule every condition is ANDed (e.g. "HA5* callsign and OC continent" never matches). Use separate rules for independent conditions.
alerts.queryHint: Same syntax as the Spots search box; combined (AND) with the fields above. re:PATTERN is a regex over the callsign/comment — e.g. re:/MM$ for maritime-mobile.
users.title: Users
raw.title: Raw terminal
raw.note: The GUI covers every function — this tab is for advanced users, for any cluster command.
raw.jumpLatest: scroll to the latest output (auto-follow paused while scrolled up)
spots.menu.prepQso: Prepare a QSO in the logger
rig.chipHint: Radio VFO (via rigctld) — click for CAT settings
conn.catHint: Drive the rig over Hamlib's rigctld: click a spot to put the radio on it. Network mode talks to a running rigctld; Serial mode starts one for your rig. Off unless you enable it here.
conn.catPoll: poll VFO frequency (show it in the top bar)
conn.catFollow: follow radio — highlight the spot nearest the rig's frequency
conn.catDigiModeHint: Which mode a digital-mode spot switches the rig to. CW and SSB spots are unaffected.
conn.logHint: Click a spot to pre-fill your logger's entry window over UDP — nothing is saved from here. “WSJT-X protocol” suits QLog / JTAlert / GridTracker / Log4OM; “bare ADIF” suits simpler Log4OM-style listeners.
conn.logFormatWsjtx: pre-fill entry window (WSJT-X protocol) — QLog, JTAlert, GridTracker, Log4OM
conn.logRaise: bring the logger window to the front after a push
spots.jumpLatest: jump to the newest spots (auto-follow paused while scrolled down)
conn.logRaiseHint: The logger's window title (e.g. “QLog”, “Log4OM”). If that doesn't raise it, try its app-id (e.g. “io.github.foldynl.QLog”, from `flatpak list`). The app picks the right method for your OS.
